title: KV cache hook entropy - personal debug log
content:
Quick summary:
- Noticing intermittent drops in trace-span arrival and metric ingestion for the obs-ingest service between 22:00-02:00 PST. Symptoms: missing spans in Tempo for some requests, Grafana view shows a 30-60s gap in per-route request count and a correlated delta in KV cache hit ratio.
- Hypothesis: a race between KV cache eviction and trace-hook enrichment causes hooks to fail fast; failures are swallowed and do not surface as errors, so metrics appear to 'drop' instead of spike.

Timeline & evidence (rough):
- 2025-11-02 21:45 PST: first user report (mobile app) about slow completions for chat features.
- 2025-11-03 00:12 PST: Grafana alert fired (ingest.route_count < 10 for 30s) from rule 'obs.ingest.route-count-drop'.
- 2025-11-03 00:13 PST: quick check in Tempo: span ids for incoming requests absent for a subset of request-ids (sampled request ids below).
- 2025-11-03 00:17 PST: increased tracing sampling from 1% -> 10% to capture more evidence; confirm missing enrichment spans correlate with redis SET/GET timeouts.

Commands & queries I ran (copied from shell history):
- kubectl -n obs logs deploy/obs-ingest -c ingest --since=30m | rg "hook|kv|error" -nA3
- kafka-console-consumer --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --topic obs-raw-logs --from-beginning --max-messages 200 | rg "ingest.copyHook" -nA2
- redis-cli -h redis-obs-01 --no-auth-warning --raw MONITOR (short sampled window)
- gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.cluster_name=\"obs-prod\" AND textPayload:ingest' --limit 200 --project=redwood-prod --freshness=7200s
- promql (Grafana Explore): increase(rate(obs_ingest_route_count[1m])) by route
- Tempo/Jaeger: trace query for traceID starting 0x8a3f... (example below)

Sample outputs (redacted ids):
- From kubectl logs:
  2025-11-03T00:12:47Z ingest INFO route=/v1/chat request_id=8ba2.. hook=kv-cache GET redis-obs-01: timeout after 1500ms; proceeding without enrichment
  2025-11-03T00:12:47Z ingest DEBUG request_id=8ba2.. sampled=false hook=trace-enricher skipped due to missing-kv

- From redis MONITOR (sample):
  00:12:47.123514 [0 10.0.0.55:53920] "GET" "kv:session:abcd1234"
  00:12:47.174001 [0 10.0.0.55:53920] "GET" "kv:session:abcd1234"
  00:12:47.175210 [0 10.0.0.55:53920] "SET" "kv:session:abcd1234" "{...}" EX 3600
  // timing shows repeated GET then immediate SET attempts -> possible evict+recompute loop

- From Tempo (missing span example):
  traceID: 0x8a3f...
  spans returned: [ingest.http.receive, ingest.validate]
  spans missing: [hook.kv-lookup, hook.trace-enrich]

Observed metric deltas:
- obs_ingest_route_count per-route dropped by ~85% for /v1/chat for 35s windows during the incident.
- obs_kv_cache_hit_ratio dropped from 0.72 -> 0.15 concurrently.
- obs_hook_error_count stayed near zero (we swallow errors in hook pipeline) -> this hides the real failure mode.

Immediate reproducible experiment (local):
1) Run ingest locally with small redis using docker-compose (redis configured with small maxmemory=64mb and volatile-lru).
2) Run a load loop to hammer same session keys -> observe eviction pattern and measure hook timings.
3) Reproduce failure with lower tracing sampling to confirm that missing spans correlate with eviction loop.

Commands to repro locally (notes):
- docker-compose -f docker/local-ingest.yml up --build
- ./scripts/load-test -c 200 -q 50 --route /v1/chat --session-key abcd1234
- redis-cli config set maxmemory 64mb; config set maxmemory-policy volatile-lru
- tail -f logs/ingest.log | rg "kv-cache|hook|timeout"

Hypotheses (prioritized):
A) Eviction/recompute loop: large numbers of simultaneous requests for cold keys cause repeated GET -> miss -> SET -> subsequent GET races; KV lookups time out intermittently. Hook code marks enrich as optional and skips trace enrichment silently.
B) Backpressure/worker saturation: when KV lookups block (redis latency), ingest worker pool queues up and the tracing hook sampling threshold logic drops enrichment work under load.
C) Network path flakiness limited to redis pod AZ during nightly compaction job; manifests as increased latencies and timeouts.
D) Metrics/ingest relay bug: a separate agent (metrics forwarder) aggregates per-route counts and occasionally misses batches when the job is OOM-killed; this explains the gap in Grafana but not missing spans.

Why A is plausible: logs show repeated GET/SET pattern and the cache hit ratio collapse correlates in time with missing spans. Also fetch timeouts observed ~1500ms which is our internal hook threshold.

Mitigations to try (short-term):
- Increase hook timeouts from 1500ms -> 3000ms to reduce swallow rate and surface more errors (make errors visible by incrementing obs_hook_error_count).
- Temporarily raise tracing sampling to 50% in the affected window to collect more traces.
- Add a fast-path: if KV GET returns timeout, push trace-enrichment into background (async) rather than blocking main request; return early but emit a metric for 'async_enrich_triggered'.
- Add a quick dashboard panel that pairs obs_kv_cache_hit_ratio with obs_hook_error_count and ingress worker queue depth.

Longer-term (engineering):
- Rework hook pipeline to treat enrichment failures as first-class errors (increment metric and include a debug flag to surface in logs).
- Add circuit-breaker around redis access per-request-key for N ms to avoid thundering herd (token bucket per key).
- Consider local in-process LRU for hot session keys as fallback to reduce redis pressure for bursty read patterns.
- Audit where errors are swallowed: instrument code paths where hook failures are 'optional' and make the default to emit a diagnostics metric.

Notes on visibility:
- Current topology: ingest -> enrich-hooks (synchronous) -> downstream model request. When enrich-hooks skip, downstream still gets request but without enrichment spans. Because hook errors are not surfaced to SLOs, we see 'gap' in telemetry rather than error spikes.
- I want to add a 'hook_missing' tag on requests when an enrichment was skipped; that will make sampling by Grafana/Traces much easier.

Sample code pointers (where to change):
- repo: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest (pkg/hooks/kv.go, pkg/hooks/trace.go)
- candidate change: in kv.go at enrich(ctx, key) -> wrap with context.WithTimeout + metrics counter on timeout + push async fallback path.

Next steps (actionable):
- [ ] Evan: roll a canary bump to increase hook timeout to 3000ms and flip sampling to 50% for 2 hours (low-risk config change). Ticket: ENGOBS-4821 (linked).
- [ ] María: add ephemeral Grafana panel to dashboard 'obs/ingest/kv-debug' showing session-key QPS, redis-latency P50/P90, and hook_error_count.
- [ ] Samir: run local repro with docker-compose and attach logs to ENGOBS-4821.
- [ ] Me (Asha): draft PR that emits 'hook_skipped' tag and increments obs_hook_error_count on timeout.

Misc debugging artifacts to save here:
- sampled traceIDs with missing spans: 0x8a3f..., 0x9b7c..., 0x7f12... (copied to ticket)
- redis slowlog excerpts (attached to PR)
- load-test script output (logs/2025-11-03-local-repro.txt)

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are we seeing similar patterns for other caches (embedding cache, rerank cache) or is this isolated to session KV?
- Is there a nightly job on redis nodes (compaction) that aligns with the 22:00-02:00 window across multiple days? Need infra confirmation.
- Should we adopt a global 'enrichment-failure' SLO and alert accordingly?

If I don't have time to follow-up: create a short runbook entry under Confluence 'OBS -> Runbooks -> KV-cache outage' that lists quick mitigations (increase timeout, flip sampling, create async fallback) and link the ticket.

Personal note: this feels like a classic 'hidden failure' where silence (no errors) masks the real impact. Priority: medium-high until we implement metrics for hook skips.

-- Asha
